A frozen, accepted, reproducing anchor for a version-invariant fact is a conservative citation, not a defective one.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-eight attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 6d74561a at 0444, 12973 bytes, unmoved; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head; required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified and matching their pins; all ten recordedInputs files reproduce with basedOn cross-checked at zero disagreements. The protected distinction resolves to two readings of one DR-131 NT-3 class rather than two NT numbers. G25 v2's namedCorpusClasses holds a single NT-3 entry with corpusTakesBothReadings true and a cells array of NT-3.missing-required-rung, reading register-claim, and NT-3.universe-unconstructible, reading v2-input, with a readingNote saying a fixture author must pin both. The join carries those two ids in two places, both byte-exact against the source cells and both unchanged from v1; namedClassesThisGate is one class; summary.ntReadingsCollapsed is false; and the distinction survives upstream too, since g25-input-corpus.v1 carries one state per reading and says 'Two cells of one class, not two NT numbers.' The separate NT-3 collision — DR-131's here against DR-133's at G23 — is handled as row-local in the registerRowNote and the sibling role, with G23 appearing only there, in the remeasurementClause, and in an explicit refusal. I tested the two defect shapes I filed earlier today, structurally rather than by reading, by first enumerating the harness's actual keys. G25 v2 has no namedCorpusNotAuthored, no leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded and no leftoverNameNote — and the join asserts none of them, at zero occurrences each, while naming namedCorpusClasses, the field its content really comes from. That omission is the most informative thing in the file: the five sibling joins for G16, G18, G21, G22 and G23 all assert leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded in their harness-spec reason, and under a shape-matching review its absence here would read as a gap. Measured against the source it is correct, and it is the clearest evidence the template was adjusted rather than copied. The G23 defect shape is likewise absent — 'catalog' occurs zero times and the predecessor role reads named-corpus, mapping to a real obligation on frozen v1. The rest holds: cell [7] of the DR-G25 row is OPEN and cell [4] is byte-identical to liveGateOwners; the corpus phrase agrees across four places including file 08; D-151's adopted text owns DR-131 NT-3 only and closes its leftover-design with remainder at G25 execution, which the join states without reopening and without taking NT-5/6/7/8; and the join pins the right harness version, v2 at ACCEPT 0/0, where v1 carries a REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The successor diff is surgical — five obligations to six, one added, none removed, doesNot byte-identical at sixteen entries, readings untouched. One judgement recorded: the sibling pin points at g23-leftover-join.v1 while that family now runs to v3. I declined to report it, because every word of the role is true of v1 and the cited fact is version-invariant — I confirmed v3 still carries NT-3 and NT-5 on DR-133 — so a frozen, accepted, reproducing anchor is a conservative citation rather than a defective one. Disclosure: every Claude-lane verdict this join pins is mine, including the harness v1 rejection that made v2 live.
